feedback: If a learner reads a single correlation as proof, ask whether another continent shows the same pattern and whether timing alone distinguishes cause from coincidence.
If a learner says the toolkit produces a true mammoth, point to the gaps in the diagram: degraded, incomplete DNA means engineering a cold-adapted elephant hybrid, not reviving the original.
Reinforce that 'combination' is a legitimate, evidence-supported answer, not a failure to choose.
activities.intendedInsight: Competing causal hypotheses can be weighed against actual evidence (timing correlations across landmasses), and the data often support interacting causes rather than a single villain.
learnerActions: On a map/timeline per continent, overlay human-arrival dates, climate records for the relevant period (including, but not only, end-of-Ice-Age warming), and the timing of megafauna decline.

Judge where the patterns fit the overkill hypothesis, where they fit the climate hypothesis, and where a combination best explains the data, using a balance meter that weighs overkill vs climate vs combination.
Write a short claim naming, for a chosen continent, which evidence pattern you find most convincing and why, and state what evidence would change your mind.
Use a 'de-extinction toolkit' diagram that lays out the genetic steps and the gaps between them to explain why recovered DNA does not yield an exact clone.
activities.title: Weigh the evidence: continent timelines of humans, climate and extinction

feedback: If a learner expects to recover dinosaur DNA, explain that DNA breaks down over time and the oldest DNA recovered so far is about 1–2 million years old, so none is expected to survive from non-avian dinosaurs, which died out at least 66 million years ago.

When you reach the ethics question, build and defend a reasoned position with at least one argument for and one against rather than searching for a single correct answer — an open ethical debate is not settled by a marked right/wrong response, so take it into the argument-construction activities.
activities.intendedInsight: Confirms secure recall of the hypotheses, evidence and DNA facts that the evaluative work builds on.
learnerActions: Match each line of evidence to the hypothesis it supports (overkill, climate, or consistent with both).
State the two main hypotheses for megafauna extinction (Tier A).
Cite one line of evidence for each hypothesis and explain what ancient DNA can tell us, and why no dinosaur DNA survives (Tier B).

Take the ethics question into the dialogue or a short written argument: construct a reasoned position with at least one strong argument for and one against, and name remaining uncertainty (Tier C) — rather than selecting a single 'right' answer.
activities.title: Factual-recall check (use only for the knowledge layer)
